q: Why does non-cyclic photophosphorylation need two photosystems (the Z-scheme)?
options: PSII makes the ATP and PSI makes the glucose, so both are needed to complete photosynthesis in light
Two photosystems are needed to split two water molecules at exactly the same time
One light boost can't lift electrons from water high enough to reduce NADP, so they're excited twice
PSI absorbs light only at night, so PSII is needed to keep photosynthesis going by day
explanation: Water holds its electrons very tightly, while reducing NADP+ requires electrons at a high energy level. PSII raises electrons from water part of the way – energy released as they pass down the ETC pumps H+ for ATP synthesis – then PSI re-energises them enough to reduce NADP+ via ferredoxin. Drawn as an energy diagram, the path zig-zags like a 'Z'.
